newsitem.title: USA: Gander Mountain plan cleared by court.
newsitem.headline: Gander Mountain plan cleared by court.

text.p: Gander Mountain Inc said Tuesday it received clearance from the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Milwaukee, Wis., to send its reorganization plan, ballots and disclosure statement to creditors and shareholders for review and approval.

It said terms call for the company's 12 retail stores and substantially all related assets of the business to be transferred to Holiday Cos, which would pay a purchase price equal to all secured debt, administrative expenses of the bankruptcy and priority claims, plus $19.5 million.

Gander Mountain said $18.5 million will be distributed among unsecured creditors, $500,000 paid pro rata to Gander Mountain preferred shareholders and $500,000 paid pro rata to holders of Gander Mountain common stock.
The reorganization plan now faces a review and comment period of about one month. A hearing on confirmation of the plan is scheduled for January 23.

If holders of the preferred oppose the plan and it cannot be confirmed by the court, there will be no distribution to preferred and common shareholders, and the amount available to unsecured creditors will increase to $19 million.

Undsecured claims of $1,000 or less, and claims that creditors reduce voluntarily to $1,000, will receive a one-time payment of 80 percent of their claims out of the funds available to unsecured creditors.
After this payment, the balance will be distributed pro rata to other unsecured creditors with allowed claims.
Gander Mountain is a specialty retailer serving the outdoor recreation market.
